terms.definition: Choosing sample sites using random numbers so that every part of the study area has an equal chance of being sampled.
terms.examiner: Use it where there is no environmental gradient. Say how: a grid and random number coordinates.

terms.definition: Taking samples at regular intervals, usually along a transect.
terms.examiner: Use it where conditions change along a gradient, such as distance from a road or up a shore.

terms.definition: How consistent results are: reliable results are similar when the investigation is repeated.
terms.examiner: More samples, standardised methods and controlling other variables improve reliability.

terms.definition: A measure of how spread out the values are around the mean.
terms.examiner: A small standard deviation means the mean is more reliable; overlapping standard deviations suggest a difference may not be significant.

terms.definition: The statement that there is no significant difference or correlation between the sets of data.
terms.examiner: Write it before the test, then accept or reject it by comparing the test value with the critical value.

terms.definition: A result is significant when the probability that it arose by chance is below the chosen level, usually 5% (p < 0.05).
terms.examiner: Say "less than 5% probability that the difference is due to chance", not that the result is "proved".

terms.definition: A factor kept the same so that it does not affect the dependent variable.
terms.examiner: Name the variable and say how it would be kept constant.

terms.definition: A result that does not fit the pattern of the others.
terms.examiner: Repeat it; do not include it in the mean unless the repeat confirms it.
